cards.title: Chameleons don't change color to hide from predators
cards.body: Contrary to popular belief, chameleons do not shift shades to blend into whatever background they sit on. Their specialized skin cells, called iridophores, rearrange microscopic nanocrystals primarily to regulate body temperature and communicate with rivals or potential mates. A cold chameleon turns dark to absorb heat, while a threatened male flashes vivid, high-contrast patterns to warn off competitors. Camouflage is merely a passive byproduct of their natural resting green or brown colors.

cards.title: The shortest war in history was over before lunchtime
cards.body: On the morning of August 27, 1896, the United Kingdom and the Sultanate of Zanzibar fought the shortest war in recorded history. After the sudden death of the pro-British sultan, an unapproved successor seized the throne and refused to step down. When a British ultimatum expired at 9:00 a.m., Royal Navy warships opened fire on the wooden palace. By approximately 9:40 a.m., the palace was in ruins and the conflict was officially over in under 45 minutes.

cards.title: A headless chicken survived for 18 months
cards.body: In September 1945, Colorado farmer Lloyd Olsen attempted to butcher a five-and-a-half-month-old rooster named Mike for dinner. Olsen's axe severed most of the bird's head but left the jugular vein, brainstem, and one ear intact. Because basic reflexes, breathing, and heart rate are managed by the brainstem, Mike survived. Olsen fed him water, milk, and mash with an eyedropper, turning the headless rooster into a touring sideshow sensation for a year and a half.

cards.title: The human body actually glows in the dark
cards.body: Every human being constantly emits visible light, though you need high-precision equipment to see it. In 2009, Japanese researchers used ultra-sensitive cryogenic cameras to image the human body in total darkness. They discovered that our bodies produce a faint glow that peaks in the late afternoon and is brightest on the face. This bioluminescence is a byproduct of cellular metabolism reacting with free radicals, but it shines roughly 1,000 times dimmer than human eyes can detect.

cards.title: Lightning strikes the same place twice all the time
cards.body: The old idiom claiming lightning never strikes the same place twice is dangerous folklore. In reality, lightning follows the path of least electrical resistance, meaning tall, isolated, and conductive structures are struck repeatedly. New York City's Empire State Building is struck by lightning an average of 25 times every single year, and has been hit as many as eight times in a single 24-minute storm, acting as a giant, harmless urban lightning rod.

quizzes.question: Why do chameleons primarily change the color of their skin?
options: To mimic the color and pattern of their background
To regulate body temperature and communicate with others
To frighten prey before striking with their tongues
To signal to their offspring that food is nearby
quizzes.explanation: Chameleons adjust microscopic nanocrystals in their skin primarily to manage body heat and signal social intent, not for background camouflage.

quizzes.question: Approximately how long did the 1896 Anglo-Zanzibar War last before the sultanate surrendered?
options: About 40 minutes
Nearly 3 days
Around 2 weeks
Exactly 4 hours
quizzes.explanation: Lasting roughly 38 to 45 minutes, the conflict ended after British naval gunfire destroyed the sultan's palace.

quizzes.question: How was Mike the chicken able to survive for 18 months after losing his head?
options: His brain fully regenerated over the following weeks
His brainstem and jugular vein were left intact by the axe
Chickens do not require blood circulation to breathe
His spinal cord developed replacement sensory organs
quizzes.explanation: Because vital functions like breathing and heart rate are controlled by the brainstem, Mike survived after the farmer's blade missed it.

quizzes.question: Why can't people see the visible light naturally emitted by the human body?
options: It is only emitted in the ultraviolet spectrum
It is about 1,000 times dimmer than human eyes can detect
It is only released while a person is asleep
It is absorbed immediately by clothing and melanin
quizzes.explanation: While humans produce true visible light through metabolic reactions, it is roughly 1,000 times too faint for the unaided eye to see.

quizzes.question: On average, roughly how many times per year is the Empire State Building struck by lightning?
options: About 25 times
Exactly once
Over 500 times
About 250 times
quizzes.explanation: The National Weather Service notes that the Empire State Building is struck an average of 25 times annually.

guesses.explanation: The entire conflict lasted under 45 minutes, with firing ceasing after roughly 38 minutes.

guesses.prompt: How many months did Mike the Headless Chicken survive after his head was chopped off?
guesses.explanation: Fed with an eyedropper by his owner, Mike survived for 18 months because his brainstem remained undamaged.

guesses.prompt: About how many times is the Empire State Building struck by lightning each year?

misconceptions.claim: Chameleons change their skin color to match their surroundings for camouflage.
misconceptions.explanation: Chameleons change color primarily to regulate body temperature and communicate social signals like aggression or mating readiness.

misconceptions.claim: The human body naturally glows in the dark with visible light.
misconceptions.explanation: Metabolic reactions involving free radicals produce visible light from our bodies, though it is 1,000 times too faint for our eyes to detect.

misconceptions.claim: Lightning never strikes the same place twice.
misconceptions.explanation: Lightning frequently strikes tall, conductive landmarks multiple times; the Empire State Building is hit about 25 times a year.
